html:
The Woodland Cree, or Sakāwithiniwak, are a Cree people of the northern forests of Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba. They speak the "th" dialect of Cree, an Algonquian language, and are the largest Indigenous group in northern Alberta.

Before the 1700s their country lay west of Hudson Bay. When the Hudson's Bay Company built posts on the bay, they became middlemen, carrying furs from peoples further west to the posts and trading guns and metal goods back. Guns let them push west and north, driving out Dene peoples. They lived by hunting moose and caribou, trapping and fishing, travelling by canoe in summer and on snowshoes in winter. Epidemics of smallpox in 1781 hit them hard. Their kin on the prairies are the Plains Cree.
